A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TDSM work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. All 11 pages of v1 and 10 pages of v3 were inspected. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDSM recognition results on NTU-60, NTU-120 and PKU-MMD, plus loss and timestep ablations and inference-noise analysis in Tables 1–4 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds text-feature and training-noise ablations in Tables 4 and 6.

M1.justification: The base TDSM procedure retains its skeleton/text encoders, global and local text conditioning, diffusion-plus-triplet objective and single-step noise-distance inference. v3 clarifies random negative-label selection and describes the DiT adaptation more briefly; neither establishes a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate zero-shot skeleton action recognition on NTU-60, NTU-120 and PKU-MMD with the same SynSE, PURLS and SMIE benchmark coverage. The new ablations manipulate existing components without adding datasets, domains or task scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in both benchmark tables. Table 1 retains ReViSE, JPoSE, CADA-VAE, SynSE, SMIE, PURLS, SA-DVAE and STAR; Table 2 retains the same set excluding PURLS. The new comparisons are internal ablations.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled experiments using only global or only local text features, and fixed Gaussian noise during both training and inference. Retained benchmark splits, metrics, encoder assignments, training budgets and inference timestep remain unchanged. Omitted architecture settings are lost documentation, not evidence of changed settings.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens validation of central design choices through two new ablation questions: whether global and local text features contribute complementary information, and whether resampling training noise benefits generalization (Tables 4 and 6). Both span four NTU splits. The existing loss, total-timestep and inference-noise analyses remain.

E5.justification: v3 removes v1's disclosure that the random seed was fixed at 2,025. Both retain averaging over 10 Gaussian-noise realizations, the inference-noise variation plot and averaging across three SMIE splits. No increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation practice is reported.

E6.justification: New ablation outcomes appear in v3 Tables 4 and 6. For NTU-60 55/5, global-only and local-only accuracy is 83.41% and 83.33%, versus 86.49% combined; fixed training noise yields 76.40%, versus 86.49% with random noise. All matched benchmark, loss-ablation, timestep-ablation and inference-sensitivity results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3 adds explicit Gaussian forward and reverse transition distributions and their connection to the variational training objective. It also omits v1's explicit CrossDiT projection, modulation and attention formulas (Equations 8–11). The central loss and inference equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first diffusion-based framework for zero-shot skeleton action recognition, discriminative skeleton-text matching through TD loss, and the same benchmark advantages. Calling the loss 'reformulated' instead of 'novel' refines wording: its inspiration from conventional triplet loss was already acknowledged in v1.

C2.justification: v3 explains global features as supplying sentence-level semantics and local features as distinguishing subtle action differences. It interprets the fixed-noise ablation as overfitting particular noise patterns and explicitly characterizes the retained single-step inference as efficient. The broader regularization rationale and inference-noise limitation already appear in v1.

D1.justification: v3 removes the detailed CrossDiT specification and discloses fewer reproducibility settings: the 12 blocks and heads, 768-dimensional features, 35 text tokens, single skeleton token and CLIP-ViT-H/14 identity disappear. It also omits the precise SA-DVAE feature/prompt provenance and PURLS encoder-training distinction. Random negative-label selection is newly specified, but substantial implementation information is lost.

R1.justification: v3 removes the entire supervised skeleton-action-recognition survey from v1 Section 2.1, substantially narrowing coverage of recurrent, convolutional, graph and transformer approaches. Associated references and the attention/modulation references supporting CrossDiT are removed. The zero-shot and diffusion positioning remains, with no new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction undergo substantial rewriting, including moving the shared-movement explanation into the introduction. v3 removes a related-work subsection, inserts a dedicated diffusion-preliminaries section and compresses the architecture explanation. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond routine editing or renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 removes the CrossDiT block diagram from v1 Figure 3 and adds two ablation tables. Retained tables are repositioned or resized and captions revised. The training and inference diagrams and sensitivity plots retain their visual content; the overall two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: v3's new ablations strengthen evidence for complementary text features and random training noise, while the preliminaries improve accessibility. However, it removes the explicit CrossDiT specification and important architecture, encoder and feature-provenance details without an appendix replacement. With benchmark evidence unchanged, this loss of information needed to understand and reproduce the core method outweighs the supporting additions, producing a limited overall decline.
